findings.title: stripe_webhook_handler_ai_credits_spec.rb fails 17/17 on stale column name amount_cents_paid (KNOWN)
findings.evidence: All 17 failures share this one signature (verified: 17/17 occurrences in /tmp/qa-run-5-layer-4/batch-b.txt) and fire in spec setup at OrganizationAiCreditPurchase.create! before any feature code runs. Root cause verified at the schema level via `rails runner`: OrganizationAiCreditPurchase.column_names includes 'stripe_amount' (true) and NOT 'amount_cents_paid' (false). The renaming commit c2f69130d (migration 20260611120002) is an ancestor of the branch BASE a0d59115d — confirmed with `git merge-base --is-ancestor c2f69130d a0d59115d` (exit 0). The spec file is byte-identical across a0d59115d..33dffbe3e (`git diff --name-only` returns empty). Matches the documented known-pre-existing entry exactly.

findings.title: organization_ai_credits_lifecycle_spec.rb:33 credit allocation mismatch (KNOWN, mode UNCHANGED)
findings.error: Failure/Error: expect(organization.organization_ai_credit_balance.monthly_credits_remaining).to eq PlanFeatureGate::MINIMUM_AI_CREDIT_ALLOCATION — expected: 25, got: 0 (at spec line 37)
findings.evidence: Failure MODE is identical to the documented one. IMPL-REVIEW-COMPLETE.md:22 records it as 'known pre-existing failure, mode unchanged' and impl-round-1/test-coverage-and-ghost-tests.md:11 pins it as '3 examples, 1 failure at :33 ... value comparison at line 37' — this run reproduces exactly that: a value comparison at line 37, expected 25 got 0. Traced chain: spec:37 -> Organization#create_ai_credit_state_if_needed (app/models/organization.rb:192-207) -> PlanFeatureGate#monthly_ai_credit_allocation (app/services/plan_feature_gate.rb:133-135) -> plan_rules 'plan_no_plan' monthly_ai_credit_allocation: 0 (plan_feature_gate.rb:149). Because 0 is truthy in Ruby, the `|| MINIMUM_AI_CREDIT_ALLOCATION` fallback never fires. The org is not stripe_subscription_in_good_standing, so @plan collapses to 'plan_no_plan' (plan_feature_gate.rb:27). NOT feature-caused: the feature's only organization.rb hunks are at lines 1131 and 1139 (`git diff -U0` hunk headers), ~930 lines away from create_ai_credit_state_if_needed; plan_feature_gate.rb and organization_ai_credit_balance.rb are absent from the feature diff.

findings.title: plan_feature_gate_ai_credits_spec.rb — 4 failures from plan_rules/Variables drift (NOT on the known list; proven pre-existing)
findings.error: 4 failures: 'returns 25 credits for plan_no_plan' expected 25 got 0; 'returns 25 credits for plan_simple_ats_free' expected 25 got 0; 'returns 250 credits for plan_ats_tier_scale' expected 250 got 150; 'returns 250 credits for plan_ats_tier_scale_v2' expected 250 got 150
findings.evidence: Two independent drifts, neither touching feature code. (1) plan_rules hardcodes monthly_ai_credit_allocation: 0 for 'plan_no_plan' (plan_feature_gate.rb:149) and 'plan_simple_ats_free' (:157); 0 is truthy in Ruby so `plan_rules[@plan]&.dig(...) || MINIMUM_AI_CREDIT_ALLOCATION` (:134) returns 0, never the 25 the spec expects. (2) SCALE_AI_CREDIT_ALLOCATION = Variables::AI_MONTHLY_CREDIT_SCALE resolves to 150 (verified via `rails runner`: MINIMUM=25 STARTER=50 GROWTH=100 SCALE=150, sourced from config/initializers/01_variables.rb:125-128), while the spec's table expects 250. DECISIVE non-causation proof: the spec's `gate_for` helper builds an OpenStruct, not an Organization — no DB record, no ActiveRecord callbacks, so Organization#handle_after_commit and therefore CreateSubscriptionEvent cannot execute in any of these examples. Both spec/services/plan_feature_gate_ai_credits_spec.rb and app/services/plan_feature_gate.rb are absent from the feature diff file list.

findings.title: The only plausible feature regression vector — removed Discord enqueues in organization.rb — is asserted by no non-feature spec
findings.evidence: The feature deletes Discord::NotifyFreeTrialStartedJob.perform_later(id) and Discord::NotifyTrialConvertedToPaidJob.perform_later(id) from Organization#handle_after_commit (organization.rb:1131, :1139), relocating them into SubscriptionEvent#handle_after_commit_on_create. A grep of the whole spec/ tree for NotifyFreeTrialStartedJob|NotifyTrialConvertedToPaidJob|NotifySubscriptionDeletedJob returns hits ONLY inside the feature's own three specs (subscription_event_fanout_spec.rb, organization_subscription_events_spec.rb, stripe_webhook_handler_subscription_events_spec.rb). No pre-existing spec asserted those enqueues, so their relocation cannot have broken anything. The org-creating controller specs that would exercise this path (registrations, organizations, omniauth_callbacks, confirmations) all passed in batch-c.
